narrative: Lancaster W4232 (coded RC-Y) of 5 Lancaster Finishing School took off from RAF Syerston at 16:01 hrs on 17 April 1944 on a general training flight. Within minutes, while the aircraft was still climbing at around 1,000 feet, the starboard wingtip detached. The aircraft stalled, rolled, and the port wing then separated. W4232 dived into the ground near the Lock Keeper's Cottage at Hazelford Weir on the River Trent. All seven crew were killed. Eye witness Terry Harrod, then aged 8 or 9, was watching from the Lock Keeper's house with his mother as the crash unfolded. P/O Bruce Lettington Humphreys RAAF, aged 20, was the pilot.
community_connection: The project was led by Bleasby Parish Council and involved numerous volunteers from the village. The dedication ceremony was attended by family members of the fallen aircrews, veterans, and community members. The event served as a poignant reminder of the sacrifices made during the war and strengthened the bond within the Bleasby community.
